newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper stocks seen up, trading thin - dealers.
newsitem.headline: LME copper stocks seen up, trading thin - dealers.

text.p: Copper stocks on the London Metal Exchange (LME) are seen rising by about 2,000-4,000 tonnnes in thin trade as the market slowly shrugs off a New Year holiday hangover, Singapore-based metal dealers said on Friday.
Aluminium stocks may also rise by 2,000-4,000 tonnes when the LME stocks report comes out at 0900 GMT on Friday, the traders said.

"The trend of modest increases in copper should continue," a dealer for a Singapore-based metal trading firm said. "But the whole market is going to be quiet until people come back from the holidays next week."
Most metal trading offices in the city-state were practically empty because of the long holiday here. Markets were closed on Wednesday for New Year and on Thursday for Singapore's general elections.
"Trading is really dead at the moment," a trader for a European metal trading firm said.
Dealers said more copper should reach the LME warehouse in Singapore in the coming months although very little material is expected to arrive here in the short-term.
The amount of copper in the LME warehouse here reached 30,100 tonnes in last Tuesday's report, up 1,250 tonnes from the previous report on December 24.
Stocks in the LME warehouse here reached a low of 1,975 tonnes at the end of September. Some 5,000 tonnes of copper remain off-warrant here, traders said.
Three month copper prices were quoted by regional dealers at around US$2,188/93 a tonne at 0200 GMT, down slightly from the last trade in London on $2,190/95 a tonne.
Aluminium prices were seen here by dealers at 0200 GMT at around $1,558/63 a tonne, marginally easier when compared to the late London trade yesterday of $1,562/64 a tonne.
